newsitem.title: USA: American Greetings profits drop on shorter lead times.
newsitem.headline: American Greetings profits drop on shorter lead times.

text.p: American Greetings Thursday reported a drop in second-quarter profits as the nation's second largest greeting card company cut shipments to retailers in order to prevent a build-up of store inventories.
Profits fell to $11.4 million, or 15 cents a share, in the quarter from $15 million, or 20 cents a share, a year ago.

Revenues rose 8.2 percent to a record $466.5 million from $431.2 million, boosted by strength in the U.S. greeting card business and the Cleveland-based company's recent purchase of John Sands, the largest greeting card business in Australasia, from Amcor Ltd.

"However, earnings for the quarter and first half reflect the impact of the shift of sales and earnings into the second half of the year as the company continues to reduce lead times with retailers," said Morry Weiss, chairman and chief executive officer.
American Greetings is the second largest greeting card company after privately held Hallmark Cards Inc.

American Greetings said it still expects full-year earnings of $2.20 to $2.30 per share, up from $1.54 per share in the fiscal year ended Feb. 29, when it posted net income of $115 million. American Greetings' stock rose 50 cents to $26.625 on Nasdaq at mid-afternoon.
